evidence: owner.lisp:1760-1763 `(unless *fnn-owner-last-fault* (setq *fnn-owner-last-fault* (ignore-errors (format nil ...))))` runs outside any lock, and is followed by `(fnn-owner-gated (service :control) ...)` and then `(fnn-err "owner core/store fault; process stopped: ~a" condition)`.
fix: Set the first fault under the roster mutex (or with sb-ext:compare-and-swap on a holder cell). Print the fnn-err line before entering the gate, or in an unwind-protect, so it is emitted even when the gated stop re-signals.
notes: Runtime GPT-6.1-Sol: actual fnn-owner-fault-service is now an irreversible owner-mutex fence/wakeup entry, matching fnn-owner-stop-service. It never requests healthy scheduler admission after abort; first-fault capture is synchronized and late cleanup fault always reaches ACL2 monotone stop lattice. Native raw regression traps any fnn-owner-gated invocation, checks actual fault-service still returns to terminal cleanup, owner exclusion holds at lattice application, and uncertainty dominates graceful-stop escalation. Full qualified-image terminal cleanup remains pending.

Caller inspection found inherited inline owner-commit-queued-locked -> frames-job fault/fence service reentry. frames-job now signals its fn-oqw-decided typed uncertain/fault verdict to the existing surrounding boundary; held section uses classify-escape-locked and off-owner committer uses thread-escape. Actual raw schedules execute phase driver and both surrounding boundaries for success/uncertainty/fault. Direct caller inventory after this fix shows no lexical owner-held fault-service site; this is source/runtime evidence, not whole callgraph realization proof. Direct owner acquisition is explicitly declared alongside stop-service in lock contracts; no baseline growth.
reviewer: The check-then-setq at 1760-1763 is outside any lock, so two simultaneous faults can record the second fault's text instead of the first. That is cosmetic: either text names a real fault. If the gate is already aborted, fnn-owner-gated's entry handler calls fnn-owner-gate-fail-locked, which re-signals (1288-1296). The fnn-err at 1769 then never runs, and the condition escapes from inside the mux.lisp:332 handler before fnn-mux-finish. This only happens after an earlier scheduler abort has already stopped the service, so it is a secondary-path diagnostics and cleanup gap.
scenario: Two mux loops fault at the same moment (e.g. both hit a broken store image). Both see nil, and the later setq overwrites the earlier one, so the stop line that `health`/`status` and the service journal print names the second fault, not the first, contrary to the defvar's docstring. When the fault is itself a scheduler failure (aborted gate), fnn-owner-gated's entry handler calls fnn-owner-gate-fail-locked, which re-signals. The fnn-err on 1769 never runs, and the condition escapes from inside the caller's own fault handler (e.g. mux.lisp:332).
title: *fnn-owner-last-fault* 'first fault' is an unsynchronized check-then-set, and its stderr line is lost when the gate is aborted
